newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London weak on GM profits talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London weak on GM profits talk.

text.p: U.S. shares were mostly lower in Europe, after reports that auto giant General Motors had sharply reduced its fourth quarter earnings estimates.

Dealers in London, citing press reports, said GM issued a profits warning after Wall Street closed on Wednesday, cutting Q4 estimates to $0.60 a share compared with market expectations of $1.00-$1.10.

"Things are a bit nervy this morning. GM hasn't fallen too sharply yet, but once the market wakes up to the fact this is a severe profits cut, we could see some pretty nasty selling," one market maker said.

GM, which reported Q3 earnings of $0.42, was down $5/8 at $53-7/8 by 1150 GMT. Elsewhere in the sector, Ford slipped $1/4 at $31-3/4, while Chrysler eased $3/8 at $32-1/8. Profit-taking unsettled high-technology shares. IBM, which soared $7-1/8 in New York on Wednesday, was down $1/2 at $158-1/4.
Compaq slipped $1/2 at $78, after rising $6-1/4 on Wednesday.
Nike, which rose to $58-3/4 in U.S after hours trading versus an official close of $55-1/8, on news that second quarter profits had risen 81 percent, was up $1/4 at $59.
Dealers expect the Dow to open lower as investors keep an eye on GM and the automotive sector.
The S&P 500 futures contract on the Globex after hours trading system, were up 0.70 at 738.85. The U.S. March T-bond was up 3/32 at 112-5/32.
